premises.text: Proprietary per-manufacturer software locks interactive lesson content into the platform and the classroom
premises.evidence_span: your content is locked not only into your platform, but it's locked into the classroom

premises.text: Downloadable software replicated in the browser runs on any device and supports simultaneous multi-user interaction without installs
premises.evidence_span: we have managed to replicate downloadable software and put it in browser

premises.text: In-browser equation and graphing tools make computer-based math practical, ending the calculator monopoly
premises.evidence_span: Texas Instruments, your monopoly on graphing in the classroom is over

premises.text: Publishing turns any lesson into content a million people can open, interact with, embed, or download offline
premises.evidence_span: a million people can look at this simultaneously, interact with it, they each have a local copy they can work with

value.text: Interactive lessons usable on any device, by anyone, anywhere
value.evidence_span: it means it works on any device that has a browser

causal_links.evidence_span: You can't access it from home. Teachers can't access it from home.

notes: Folded reading per v1.3.2 clarification 5: device reach and simultaneous collaboration are presented as the two direct consequences of one browser-based mechanism, so they sit in a single premise; publish/sharing is grouped into the same platform domain because the speaker demos it as a feature of the same software rather than a standalone product. Funding announcement and alpha codes excluded; the publisher-built demo lesson treated as validation. Two domains: the lock-in need versus the browser platform that answers it.
